title: Phased adopter for batching & caching recommendations
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a 'phased adopter' subsystem that can safely apply suggested batching and KV/prefix caching configs from Optimize. The adopter should run policy-driven gradual activation (percentage ramps, traffic weighting, time windows), automatic health checks (latency P99, error rate, token-per-second cost delta), and a simulated dry-run mode that validates output stability before any live change. We want minimal manual toil for routine low-risk suggestions while preserving operator control for risky or high-impact changes.
acceptance_criteria: Can apply a suggested batching configuration to 1% of traffic and ramp to 50% using policy rules
Automatic rollback triggers when P99 latency increases > 20% or error rate > 0.5% relative to baseline
Dry-run can detect correctness regressions by replaying historical requests and comparing token/response hashes
Operator UI shows live comparison of cost delta, latency, and quality metrics during canary
Audit trail with reasoning, selected thresholds, and final decision stored in customer-level logs
tasks: Design adopter policy schema (ramp, windows, thresholds, guardrails)
Implement dry-run traffic replay library and deterministic response diffing
Integrate adopter with Optimize suggestions API and Console approvals flow
Add canary health-checker service and circuit-breaker hooks into serving runtime
Expose per-suggestion preview dashboard and cost/quality projections
Document runbook for manual intervention and post-mortem checklist
implementation_notes: Prefer non-blocking changes: adjust batching window and prefix cache percentage using runtime flags to avoid node restarts
KV cache warming strategy: prefetch hot key prefixes during canary to reduce cold-start noise
Simulated dry-run will run in parallel using mirrored requests with masked customer identifiers
Keep model routing stable; changes should only adjust batching/caching layer, not model selection
Plan to reuse existing rollout infra from 'rollouts-service' but add new predicate types for cost signals
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased P99 due to larger batches. Mitigation: enforce max latency threshold and fallback to previous config immediately
Risk: Response quality regression from cache-induced context shifts. Mitigation: utilize replay diffs and sample-based human review in early ramps
Risk: High-cost oscillation if config flips rapidly. Mitigation: hysteresis windows and cooldown between successive applies
Risk: Secrets/exposure when replaying requests. Mitigation: mask PII and run dry-run only in dedicated, access-controlled environments
rollout_plan: Step 1: Run dry-run for 48h against anonymized historical traffic (no live apply)
Step 2: Canary apply to 1% production for 2h, collect metrics and run automated diffs
Step 3: If stable, ramp to 10% over 6h with continuous checks; escalate to engineering on threshold violations
Step 4: Ramp to 50% and hold for 24h; request PM/Design sign-off for >50% or cross-model impact
Step 5: Full apply or schedule phased rollout across regions with per-region safety gates
QA_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and decision engine
E2E tests that mirror a canary scenario in staging with synthetic load generator
Replay-based correctness tests comparing responses to golden set
Chaos test: introduce synthetic latency spikes to verify automatic rollback
review_feedback: PM (Carlos Vega): prefer explicit human approval for cost savings > 25% to avoid downstream billing surprises
Design (Amaya Patel): console needs a compact metric card showing expected token delta, latency delta, and a risk score
Security (Isha Rao): ensure dry-run cannot persist PII and add KMS-protected logs for audit
Infra (Marcus Li): avoid global flags — implement per-cluster feature gates to limit blast radius
